title: The Great Fire of 8-10 October 1871: where it burned, and when
clock: Chicago local time as the accounts give it (the city kept its own mean time in 1871; railway standard time came in 1883), the same clock as the scene's hours (time-of-day.js, local mean solar time).

wind.locator: p. 727, the Times: 'the wind was blowing a gale from a southwesterly direction; and, above the tops of the buildings, its course, from midnight until 4 or 5 o'clock, varied but little'.
wind.note: The direction is the accounts'; the speed (about 27 miles an hour) is reconstructed for a 'gale' and only sets how far the smoke leans.

rain.locator: p. 757: 'The rain, which began about eleven o'clock Monday night, effected a perceptible check on the flames.'
rain.note: After the rain the flames die down over about three hours and nothing new catches; the ruins smoulder on.

conversion.method: Modern latitude and longitude of the 1871 street corners and places named below are carried into the scene's local east/north metres by an affine fit to the modern OpenStreetMap controls of data/context/1871/plan.json (the same controls the 1871 city's map alignment rests on). Rivers and the lake shore are the scene's own (data/terrain/epochs/e1871_prefire).

zones.name: The West Division, from the O'Leary barn north to Van Buren Street and east to the South Branch
zones.note: The fire ran north and east from the barn between Jefferson Street and the river (Andreas pp. 717-718: the houses on the west side of Jefferson Street stood; its two columns between Clinton and Jefferson and between Clinton and Canal). Its south edge is DeKoven Street at the barn and its north edge Van Buren Street, against the ground the Saturday fire had cleared. The Board gives about 160 acres for the West Division.

zones.name: The South Division, from the South Branch to the lake, north of Taylor and Congress streets to the main river
zones.note: Andreas pp. 738-740: the line of ruin ran from Harrison Street to the main river, and the fire was stopped at Harrison Street between State Street and Wabash Avenue (the block between Congress, Harrison, State and Wabash given up) and along Congress Street from Wabash Avenue to the lake. South of Harrison it burned back along the river to about Taylor Street (Andreas p. 720, the fire 'which reached Polk Street at a later hour than one o'clock'; Conzen's plate C2), held on the east by the railroad tracks by Clark Street. The Board gives nearly 500 acres for the South Division.

controls.label: The O'Leary barn, DeKoven Street
controls.locator: Andreas p. 719, 'At 8:45 the incipient blaze began'; the Board: flames seen 'not more than twenty or twenty-five minutes past nine', the alarm 'at 9:30'.
controls.note: Nine o'clock, between Andreas's 8:45 and the Board's 9:20.
controls.plan_note: The O'Leary lot as T-3689 builds it on the 1871 plan's DeKoven Street (data/structures/oleary_cottage_1871.json, oleary_barn_1871.json): the plan, a tracing of Mitchell's 1870 map, has DeKoven Street about 35 m north of where the modern controls put it here, so the fire starts in the barn the scene stands.

controls.locator: Andreas p. 720: 'the back-setting of the fire, which reached Polk Street at a later hour than one o'clock'; plate C2: an origin marked 2:30 a.m. south of Harrison Street by the river.

controls.label: The Palmer House, State and Quincy
controls.locator: p. 739: at four o'clock 'the Palmer House the only first-class hotel' left; p. 726, it 'fell at nearly the same time as the Academy of Design', after the Bigelow House fell as 'the day was fully ushered in'.

controls.label: Dearborn and Jackson, the renewal at seven
controls.locator: p. 739, Sheahan: 'At about seven o'clock in the morning, a sudden gust of wind swept and eddied through Dearborn Street, beginning at Jackson ... All that had been left untouched between Jackson and Madison streets, from Dearborn Street to the lake shore, was doomed'.

st_michaels_church_1871.note: Burned out; its walls stood and the church was rebuilt within them.

chicago_pumping_station_1871.note: Andreas p. 742: the roof caught at 3:20 and fell on the engines; the stone walls stood.

burning_by.note: Andreas p. 742, D. W. Fuller: the brand struck the engine house and 'In an instant, the roof was aflame'; 'exactly twenty minutes past three'.

oleary_barn_1871.note: A frame barn: burned to the ground.

burning_by.note: Burning at nine, when the jaunt's first stop stands before it: Andreas p. 719, 'At 8:45 the incipient blaze began'; the Board's witnesses saw the flames by twenty past nine. The fire's own clock starts at nine, so the barn is drawn alight when it starts.

cook_county_court_house_1871.note: Andreas p. 719: the bell fell at 2:05; the stone walls stood as a shell.

burning_by.note: Andreas p. 719: 'At 1:30, the men in the tower barely escaped with their lives'; pp. 724-725, Schaffer left the building at half-past one, the tower alight.
Sheahan and Upton pp. 76-77: after the Court House dome fell, 'The Sherman House was the next to go'; Andreas p. 725 puts the bell's fall at five past two (the jaunt's sherman-hour claim).

Colbert and Chamberlin p. 207: the column turned east from the Court House and Crosby's fell 'rapidly before it', some minutes after the bell's fall at five past two (Andreas p. 725; the jaunt's crosbys-hour claim).

Horace White (Andreas pp. 734-735) saw the store's own pumps 'showering that massive pile of pure marble and iron' after daylight, and the streams stopped when he came back from breakfast; Sheahan and Upton p. 79: it 'soon yielded'; Colbert and Chamberlin pp. 209-210 take the fire from the Tribune to Potter Palmer's store. About eight (the jaunt's field-hour claim). The blocks round it burned in the night (the field_leiter control); the store held under its own water until morning.
The jaunt's tribune-hour claim: Bross found it safe at daybreak and the fire back upon it that morning (Andreas pp. 731-732); Colbert and Chamberlin p. 209 give half-past seven.

st_pauls_church_1871.note: Andreas p. 717: a wooden church, 'gone down in ruins' by ten.

dalton_cottage_1871.note: Andreas vol. 2, p. 708: the fire went from the barn to the adjoining sheds, barns and dwellings to the north and north-east within minutes; a frame cottage burned to the ground.

dalton_shed_1871.note: A board shed beside the barn, joined to it by a high fence (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 708, 712).

forbes_cottage_1871.note: A frame house two doors east of the barn, in the fire's path north and east.

cemetery_dead_house_1871.note: The cemetery's dead-house, burned on Monday evening among the refugees: 'It burns until it is consumed' (Colbert and Chamberlin, p. 267).

washington_square_1871.note: The square's wooden fence and the goods left on its grass burned (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759).

model.interpolation: A place's hour is read linearly across a Delaunay triangulation of the timed places in its own division (no triangle spans a river), laid out with the across-wind distance stretched 1.8 times (the fire ran down the wind from the south-west); beyond the outermost timed places it takes the nearest edge's hours. Each building adds up to six minutes either way of its own seeded jitter. Interpolated hours are inferred; the jitter is reconstructed.
model.note: How long a building burned and when it fell is reconstructed: frame houses burned through in about half an hour, the 'fire-proof' business blocks of stone and brick held their walls while their floors and roofs burned out over about an hour (Andreas p. 720, 'Stone, brick and wooden structures fell alike'). About a third of the masonry walls are brought down.

goods.label: The furniture of the families who fled into Washington Square
goods.locator: Sheahan and Upton pp. 209-211: 'this park early in the night was filled with fugitives and their furniture'; 'In front was the grand blaze from the accumulated furniture of fifty families.' Andreas vol. 2, p. 759: the square's fence and the goods on its grass burned.
goods.note: That the square was filled with furniture and that it burned is the accounts'; how many heaps, where each lies and what is in it (chairs, tables, bedsteads, bureaus, trunks, mattresses, bundles) is reconstructed (L-1871-great-fire-goods-3751). The heaps burn at the square's own hour, read from the fire's map, and by midday lie charred and smoking. They are drawn on the square from half past two, when the fire crossed the main river (the jaunt's north-side stop), the hour the families began to come in being reconstructed.

goods.label: Beds, chairs and bundles carried into the old City Cemetery
goods.locator: Colbert and Chamberlin pp. 265-268: the refugees in Lincoln Park and the old cemetery were 'compelled to see the household gods and valuables which they had moved into the cemetery or the park burn up before their eyes.'
goods.note: That goods were carried in and some burned is the account's; the number of heaps, where they lie, what is in them, which of them burn (two in five) and when, between ten past five and twenty to seven on Monday evening, are reconstructed (L-1871-great-fire-goods-3751). The cemetery itself is a survivor; only these goods burn. They are drawn in the cemetery from six on Monday morning, a reconstructed hour inside the day the North Side fled north.
